Send keys from the project's .env to the instance's script variables, asking before each.

Values are never shown: not in the questions, the output, --json or an error. Keys are read from the
file only, never from your shell's environment. The instance shows values masked, so a key it
already has is replaced without knowing whether the value differs.

Usage: hpy happyview env push [OPTIONS] [KEY]...

Arguments:
  [KEY]...
          Only these keys; each must be in the file (default: every key in it)

Options:
      --json
          Print the result as JSON on stdout

      --url <URL>
          The instance, e.g. https://api.example.com (default: HPY_HV_URL, else the only one you are
          signed in to)

      --env-file <PATH>
          Read the keys from this file instead of .env in the project root

      --no-input
          Never prompt; fail when a value is missing. Irreversible actions still need --yes. Implied
          without a terminal

  -C <DIR>
          Run as if started in DIR

      --dry-run
          List each key as new or replacing an existing one, and send nothing

  -y, --yes
          Send every key without asking

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
